I am a final-year undergraduate in Applied Mathematics at Beijing Normal–Hong Kong Baptist University (BNBU), graduating in June 2027. I spent Spring 2026 as an exchange student at Hong Kong Baptist University.

My research centers on scientific machine learning and numerical methods, particularly neural models for multiphase flow simulation. I also work on computer vision for archery analysis and have developed AI tools for education.

Scientific Machine LearningComputational Fluid DynamicsComputer Vision

Selected research

01 — 03
01

JAN 2026 — PRESENT SCIENTIFIC MACHINE LEARNING

Neural Curvature Estimation for Two-Phase Flow Simulations

Learning interface curvature from local level-set information, from synthetic training data to deployment in a multiphase flow solver.

  • Generated approximately 83.5 million samples across five grid resolutions.
  • Reduced MSE by factors of 5.6–260 versus second-order finite differences in matched-resolution tests.
  • Integrated standalone C inference into Basilisk’s CLSVOF solver; evaluated stationary bubble, capillary wave, and rising bubble cases.

Supervisor: Dr. Jiaqi Zhang

Python / PyTorch / C / BasiliskManuscript in preparation ↗
02

JUN 2026 — PRESENT COMPUTER VISION

Automated Arrow-Impact Localization & Ring-Score Recognition

Developing a vision pipeline for automated archery assessment, covering data curation, annotation, model training, and evaluation under practical shooting conditions.

  • Trained YOLO-based detection on public data and assessed generalization on self-collected target images.
  • The best preliminary preprocessing configuration achieved precision and recall above 70% on self-collected images.

Supervisors: Dr. Lidong Fang · Prof. Huaxiong Huang

Python / PyTorch / YOLO / OpenCV
03

JUL 2025 — MAY 2026 SCIENTIFIC COMPUTING

Data-Driven Archery Arrow Selection

Research assistant on a joint project with the 18th Institute of CASC and Beijing Institute of Technology for the Chinese National Archery Team.

  • Conducted controlled shooting experiments and shaft-deflection measurements.
  • Developed high-speed-video analysis for launch velocity, launch angle, and trajectory deviation.
  • Linked physical measurements, shot kinematics, scores, and impact locations to support quantitative arrow selection.
